messages.author: c836af6dd4dfb737
messages.subject: Study design not as planned
parts:
Hi secr users,

We recently placed 54 trap cameras spaced ±2000 meters apart with the goal to calculate the jaguar density in our study area with secr methodology. However, fieldwork did not go as planned, resulting in three grids that are separated by 4.8-5.5 km from each other. I have added an image with the resulting study design.

  1. The largest continuous grid has 35 cameras
  2. The second grid that is not connected has 9 cameras (5.5 km apart from the nearest neighboring camera of the first grid).
  3. The third grid has 10 cameras (4.8 km apart from the nearest neighboring camera the first grid).

Male jaguars have home ranges >3 times as large as female jaguars, hence there should not be any problem using all data to calculate male jaguar density. However, for female jaguars the study design might not fulfill the requirement that all individuals need to have a probability >1 to be captured. E.g. there might be an entire female territory present in the gap between grids. Am I correct in the following assumptions:

  •  Male jaguar density can be calculated using all data.
    Then what would be the influence of the large difference in spacing between camera stations of neighboring grids? Obviously, there would not be any (re)capture data within the gaps, so it would result in a smaller precision. Is there something fundamental that I’m missing?
  • Female density should first be calculated for the largest continuous grid. Might female home range turn out to be larger than 5.5 km in diameter (the spacing between different grids), all data can be used for females as well. More likely is that female home ranges are smaller than 5.5 km in diameter, which would mean we cannot use the female jaguar data without additional measures.
    a.      In the case we need additional measures. If I am right it is recommended to not run two separate analyses with male and female data separated. Because the total amount of data used in a single analysis (male and female data together) is likely to be higher although excluding data from the two smaller grids.
    b.      To include data from the smaller grids we could make three different sessions for the three different grids. We are repeating this study in different areas of the country. When analyzing data from those areas together, we would need sessions for the different locations in the country and sub-sessions for the three grids within the current location (this study). But this is not possible in the R secr library if I am right?

Thank you in advance,

Jarno Verdonk

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Study design not as planned
parts:
Hi Jarno
Why do you think  "all individuals need to have a probability >1 to be capture"? This is not a requirement of SECR, and would only be meaningful for a delimited population.
Otherwise, I don't quite know what your issue is. Small, isolated grids yield rather few recaptures. You can evaluate designs by simulation.
Murray
